title: Fix renderer bootstrap and font initialization on current Electron/Linux
body:
Related to #820

## Why

On current Linux/Electron environments, Pencil can remain stuck on the splash screen because the renderer bootstrap is fragile:

- classic renderer scripts expect globals such as `fs`, `path`, and `remote`
- font initialization relies on a `document.fonts` flow that does not complete reliably
- `FontLoader` assumes `systemRepo` is already initialized

These failures prevent the application view from being mounted.

## What changed

- explicitly expose renderer bootstrap dependencies used by legacy scripts
- keep local aliases in `app.js` so the bootstrap file itself still works
- make `FontLoader` defensive when `systemRepo` is not yet available
- switch font-face loading flow to an explicit `face.load()` based sequence

## Impact

- prevents the renderer from getting stuck on the splash screen
- reduces bootstrap-time exceptions on current Linux/Electron environments
- keeps the change scoped to renderer bootstrap and font initialization

title: Linux/Electron bootstrap leaves renderer stuck on splash because renderer globals and font loading are fragile
body:
### Summary

On a current Linux desktop, running the current `master` branch can leave Pencil stuck on the splash screen.

The main window opens, but the UI is never mounted. The renderer keeps the raw `<ui:ApplicationPane .../>` node in the DOM instead of materializing the application view.

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Branch tested: `master`
- Commit tested: `7d0ec3d`
- Electron from project dependencies

### Reproduction

1. Clone `evolus/pencil`
2. Run `npm install` at repository root
3. Run `npm install` inside `app/`
4. Start the app

### Observed behavior

- Splash stays visible
- Main UI is not mounted
- Renderer throws cascading exceptions

### Exceptions observed

Representative failures observed during renderer startup:

- missing renderer globals used by classic scripts, such as `fs`, `path`, `remote`
- font loading path using `document.fonts` in a way that does not complete reliably on current Electron/Chromium
- `FontLoader.systemRepo` being read before it is initialized

Examples from runtime inspection:

- `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'faces')`
- `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fonts')`

### Notes

This seems to be a combination of:

1. renderer bootstrap relying on globals that are no longer implicitly shared the way the rest of the code expects
2. fragile font-loading bootstrap
3. `FontLoader` assuming `systemRepo` is already available

I have a local patch that reduces this to a small set of changes in:

- `app/app.js`
- `app/pencil-core/common/FontLoader.js`
- `app/pencil-core/common/FontLoaderUtil.js`

If useful, I can turn that into a focused PR.

title: Clickable Navigation Menu doesn't show Page Name on Pop Ubuntu
Security: DOM XSS via unsanitized `innerHTML` assignment
body:
## Problem

`options.message` is written directly into `this.message.innerHTML` without sanitization. If `options.message` can be influenced by untrusted input, arbitrary HTML/JS can execute in the renderer context.

**Severity**: `high`
**File**: `app/views/common/PromptDialog.js`

## Solution

Replace `innerHTML` with `textContent` for plain text, or sanitize using a strict allowlist sanitizer before assigning HTML.

## Changes

- `app/views/common/PromptDialog.js` (modified)

## Testing

- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] Manual review completed
- [ ] No new warnings/errors introduced

title: feat: use XDG base directories via `app.getPath("userData")`, closes #174
body:
For backwards compatibility, this first checks if the current config directory `~/.pencil/` exists. If it does, it uses that.

Otherwise it uses `~/.config/Pencil/`. In fact this directory also already exists. I'm not sure why *Pencil* has 2 config directories. This PR then reduces the # of config directories to 1.

I tested this on the current release v3.1.1.

Integrate [Salt](https://plantuml.com/salt), a markup language extending PlantUML, into Pencil to enhance its functionality for creating wireframes, mockups, and demonstrative prototypes for GUIs.

- **Automation**: Users can create macros, reuse text, and automate repetitive tasks.
- **Markdown Compatibility**: It is possible to embed PlantUML inside Markdown files, providing a seamless experience for documentation and design.

title: Not clear how to use curvy or multiple-segment lines
body:
* Operating system: Ubuntu 20.04.5
* Pencil version: 3.1.0

"Line" widgets are available from the "Common Shapes" and "Flowchart" collections, in flavours like "Free Line", "Straight Connector", "Multi-Segment Connector" and "Curvy Connector". (As far as I cant tell, all of these *seem* to be the exact same thing, but with their "mode" property changed.) However, there seems to be no information in the app or on the website about how curvy or multi-segment lines can be manipulated. Is it possible to curve "around" other widgets so as to avoid them? Or to add more segments to a multi-segment connector? Attempting to use them to connect various other items seems to give fairly random results: e.g. sometimes the "curvy" connector does indeed curve, at random spots, sometimes it doesn't.

Providing some information on what these connectors are and how to use them would be useful.

title: No in-application help
body:
* Operating system: Ubuntu 20.04.5
* Pencil version: 3.1.0

The app does not seem to have any in-app help - only an "About" item on the main menu. Providing some help documentation might be useful, since there are many features not documented on the website or wiki. (E.g. How does one create a "multiple-segment" line?)

Breaking Changes

Breaking changes will be documented here, and deprecation warnings added to JS code where possible, at least one major version before the change is made.

Types of Breaking Changes

This document uses the following convention to categorize breaking changes:

  • API Changed: An API was changed in such a way that code that has not been updated is guaranteed to throw an exception.
  • Behavior Changed: The behavior of Electron has changed, but not in such a way that an exception will necessarily be thrown.
  • Default Changed: Code depending on the old default may break, not necessarily throwing an exception. The old behavior can be restored by explicitly specifying the value.
  • Deprecated: An API was marked as deprecated. The API will continue to function, but will emit a deprecation warning, and will be removed in a future release.
  • Removed: An API or feature was removed, and is no longer supported by Electron.

Planned Breaking API Changes (23.0)

Removed: BrowserWindow scroll-touch-* events

The deprecated scroll-touch-begin, scroll-touch-end and scroll-touch-edge events on BrowserWindow have been removed. Instead, use the newly available input-event event on WebContents.

// Removed in Electron 23.0
win.on('scroll-touch-begin', scrollTouchBegin)
win.on('scroll-touch-edge', scrollTouchEdge)
win.on('scroll-touch-end', scrollTouchEnd)

// Replace with
win.webContents.on('input-event', (_, event) => {
if (event.type === 'gestureScrollBegin') {
scrollTouchBegin()

body:
Bumps [async](https://github.com/caolan/async) from 0.9.2 to 2.6.4.
Release notes

Sourced from async's releases.

v2.3.0

  • Added support for ES2017 async functions. Wherever you can pass a Node-style/CPS function that uses a callback, you can also pass an async function. Previously, you had to wrap async functions with asyncify. The caveat is that it will only work if async functions are supported natively in your environment, transpiled implementations can't be detected. (#1386, #1390)

v2.2.0

  • Added groupBy, and the Series/Limit equivalents, analogous to _.groupBy (#1364)
  • Fixed transform bug when callback was not passed (#1381)

v2.1.5

  • Fix auto bug when function names collided with Array.prototype (#1358)
  • Improve some error messages (#1349)
  • Avoid stack overflow case in queue
  • Fixed an issue in some, every and find where processing would continue after the result was determined.
  • Cleanup implementations of some, every and find

v2.1.3

  • Make bundle size smaller
  • Create optimized hotpath for filter in array case.

v2.1.2

  • Fixed a stackoverflow bug with detect, some, every on large inputs (#1293).

v2.1.0

  • retry and retryable now support an optional errorFilter function that determines if the task should retry on the error (#1256, #1261)
  • Optimized array iteration in race, cargo, queue, and priorityQueue (#1253)

v2.0.0

Lots of changes here!

First and foremost, we have a slick new site for docs. Special thanks to @​hargasinski for his work converting our old docs to jsdoc format and implementing the new website. Also huge ups to @​ivanseidel for designing our new logo. It was a long process for both of these tasks, but I think these changes turned out extraordinary well.

The biggest feature is modularization. You can now require("async/series") to only require the series function. Every Async library function is available this way. You still can require("async") to require the entire library, like you could do before.

We also provide Async as a collection of ES2015 modules. You can now import {each} from 'async-es' or import waterfall from 'async-es/waterfall'. If you are using only a few Async functions, and are using a ES bundler such as Rollup, this can significantly lower your build size.

Major thanks to @​Kikobeats, @​aearly and @​megawac for doing the majority of the modularization work, as well as @​jdalton and @​Rich-Harris for advisory work on the general modularization strategy.

Another one of the general themes of the 2.0 release is standardization of what an "async" function is. We are now more strictly following the node-style continuation passing style. That is, an async function is a function that:

  1. Takes a variable number of arguments
  2. The last argument is always a callback
  3. The callback can accept any number of arguments
  4. The first argument passed to the callback will be treated as an error result, if the argument is truthy
  5. Any number of result arguments can be passed after the "error" argument
  6. The callback is called once and exactly once, either on the same tick or later tick of the JavaScript event loop.

There were several cases where Async accepted some functions that did not strictly have these properties, most notably auto, every, some, and filter.

Another theme is performance. We have eliminated internal deferrals in all cases where they make sense. For example, in waterfall and auto, there was a setImmediate between each task -- these deferrals have been removed. A setImmediate call can add up to 1ms of delay. This might not seem like a lot, but it can add up if you are using many Async functions in the course of processing a HTTP request, for example. Nearly all asynchronous functions that do I/O already have some sort of deferral built in, so the extra deferral is unnecessary. The trade-off of this change is removing our built-in stack-overflow defense. Many synchronous callback calls in series can quickly overflow the JS call stack. If you do have a function that is sometimes synchronous (calling its callback on the same tick), and are running into stack overflows, wrap it with async.ensureAsync().

Another big performance win has been re-implementing queue, cargo, and priorityQueue with doubly linked lists instead of arrays. This has lead to queues being an order of magnitude faster on large sets of tasks.

title: fix width/height is scale NaN in img for export web page
broken links in export "Clickable Prototype HTML Template" + fix
body:
* Operating system: issue discovered on Win7, fix tested under CentOS7
* Pencil version: 3.1.0

Hi to everyone...

I have a simple project thats define some behaviour as navigations between some pages at some levels - 6 on deep -
But, when the project is exported as **Clickable Prototype HTML Template**. first links works ok but the others doesnt works (note that exporting as _Default HTML template_, everything works fine, but the presentation isnt "atractive")

For now, the workarround that I found, is to remove the following rule under _Resources/style.css_ under the exported project:
```
.Page .ImageContainer > .Links > a {
    position: absolute;
    background-color: transparent;
    transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
```
So, I clone the project and made such change at [style.css](https://github.com/evolus/pencil/blob/master/app/pencil-core/templates/HTML/prototype.HTML/Resources/style.css) to test it... and seems to fix it, but I didnt promote a PR.

So, thats all

Regards
maximatt

title: fixes the calculation of alignment for dynamic width shapes
body:
This change aims to fix the behaviour of alignment for plain text type shapes (label, text box, box, etc). Previously the width for these was hardcoded at 2000 which means center and right alignment would cause the content to 'disappear' off the visible canvas.

This change allows types to define dynamic width so that alignment is calculated with respect to the longest line of content or container width, whichever is first.

See a video here for test cases and explanation: https://www.loom.com/share/db04a47c71124cf5a6d42e402f68dabc

title: Community support - proposals to help more / what do others think?
body:
* Operating system: all 
* Pencil version: all 

Hi, I have used pencil on and off for a number of years, mostly when I have small or open source ideas I want to prototype.  I really appreciate it.  Occasionally I've been involved in supporting other users.  I now realised that this is explicitly welcomed and I'd like to make some proposals to improve the way this works. 

At present it's a bit difficult to help for several reasons - 
1) it's not totally clear that this is welcome - the fact that it is so is only visible in a few tickets
2) much of the knowledge is in tickets which makes it difficult to structure and understand 

Some ideas for improvement could include
a) identify people who are willing and give them the ability to close and tag bugs so that the bug database can shrink
b) have some form of wiki and documentation of community issues and/or other form of communication for community members
c) build some form of continuous integration so that it's possible for helpers to get commits into the development tree knowing that they are reasonably safe

I think that the most important thing is to allow people to feel that they get responses about the software even when people at evolus are completely busy and don't have time.  Since everyone will be volunteers that means having quite a wide group of people involved in a more light kind of way.

title: Groups of connected shapes can't be copied without a bug
body:
* Operating system: Windows 7
* Pencil version: 3.0.4

Hi,

I tried to build an "image" shape for wireframing purpose, by connecting two free lines (with no arrows at tail ends) to the corners of a rectangle shape, to draw a cross. It worked as intended : after grouping the whole, the resizing of the final shape makes the lines to follow the corners.

Proud of this, I added the shape to my library, but when I tried to load more of one instance of that shape, a strange bug occured (wich occurs if I simply copy the loaded shape on the board too) : **the lines try to connect to the first instance of the previous loaded shape ! This making the sub-group of these lines to "outfit" the whole group to wich they belong.**

This bug makes the use of the shape impossible, or limited to one instance only, what is useless. I think that it occurs because the lines "memorized" their connections to corners in relation with the rectangle ID ; and when loading a new instance or copying the shape, the rectangle ID of the second instance is the same than the first one, and its sub-group (the lines) try to connect to the other shape because it has a kind of precedence.

In short, to fix that problem, you should find a way to generate random IDs of shapes and "update" connection locations. I gave a look at the XML of the library and found the shape, but it's too complicated for me to understand and I didn't found any "connection location" related to the master shape ID.

edit : 
I add one thing : it seems that sometimes (randomly) the shape doesn't save correctly, and just loading it on the board and trying to resize it results in a bug where connectors are lost, and sub-groups doesn't react as they should. In fact, grouping connected shapes in purpose to manipulate them doesn't seem effective.

Providing both SHA512 and SHA256 would increase the security.

title: [Feature request] Make an SCM-friendly storage format (no zip)
body:
* Operating system: irrelevant (Windows)
* Pencil version: 3.0.0-rc.2

Create a storage format that allows seeing the relevant changes in a textual diff.
At the next level, make sure that merge operations tend to "just work".

Things to consider:
- Not a compressed format.
- Store a flat list of interlinked objects, not a hierarchy (which can be represented as a list of references to subobjects).
- Users should have a way to assign meaningful names to individual screen elements. A default could be inferred from sample content; otherwise, on the screen, it should be possible to see the name of a given element, and to quickly find an element given a name (best if the names are near the objects, but that may be too cluttered).
- For coordinates, prefer "whatever the user specified" instead of pixel coordinates.

There may be more things to consider; the basic guideline would be "make it resemble how a human would want to write code to create that mockup", because that's what diff and merge tools are optimized for.

The litmus test would be to have a moderately complex screen, have two people do changes that a layman would not expect to interfere with each other, and then see whether `git merge` does something sensible with it.

No bad feelings on my side if this is closed as "cannot implement" :-)

title: support inkscape path-effect
body:
Dear pencil team,
you did an awesome work - being able to transform svg to stencils and interact with them conveniently is so great!

I want to note that pencil seems to miss inkscapes path-effect capabilities. For example you could use this for fancy graphs like BSpline path of inkscape. Here, the path ``d`` variable is always computed out of  ``inkscape:original-d`` and additional informations over the path-effect to be applied. This recomputation is not yet implemented in pencil I guess.

I tried to find some easy ways to support this recompution and found
```
inkscape -z --export-plain-svg=output.svg input.svg
```
which in fact recomputes the path-effect.  [However also deletes all path-effect informations and there seems to be no special for just reexecuting path effects without deleting their meta data. But by id you can easily extract the newly computed path ``d`` from the ouput.svg, for instance.]

Still for performance reasons it might be better to look at the source code of ``--export-plan-svg`` and reimplement it within pencil.

any feedback is highly appreciated

* Pencil version: 3 RC1

title: adapt (curvy) connectors
body:
Dear pencil team,   [this is related to #237]

the general case is that in some situations the default connectors placing doesn't fit well with the overall layout. This means for examples that the connector crosses some other objects or connectors which one may want to prevent. Or for example you want to make a curvy connector which connects two very far endings by a kind of half circle around the whole plot.

I thought that this is exactly one of the use cases the connectionPoint was made for. However it seems not possible to make a smooth half circle by combining a reasonable number of single curvy connectors and connectionPoints.
The connectionPoints already have the feature that you can decide from which side the connector shall approach the point, however if you do so, the connector is placed a good bit away from the connectionPoint, making it impossible to create a connected curvy line out of the single patches.
The only option so far to get a continuous overall line is to connect the connectors to the centre of the respective connectionPoints. However using this anchor, the lines are no longer curvy but rather resemble straight lines from connectionPoint to connectionPoint.

Suggestions:
- add a feature to adapt one single connector. E.g. the possibility to add an intermediate point where the connector has to go through, while still staying curvy (or multi-segmented).
- Enhance the connectionPoint to enable similar things
    * e.g. **having the possibility to make it transparent also when the connectors are not connected to the centre but with a specified angle.** (EDIT: this seems to be the preferred way to do it, as it is a natural feature and involves very little up to zero additional magic)
    * or when connecting multiple connectors to the centre of a connectionPoint, try to automatically compute the incoming/outcoming angle of all intermediate connector-endings (based on the final target and final source object)

I hope that this suggestion may prove useful.

* Operating system: Windows
* Pencil version: 3 RC1

title: (rectangle) selection tool
body:
Dear pencil team,

by default if you drag on empty space in the page you can draw a rectangle for selecting components.
Unfortunately this feature is prevented if you have several objects stacked, like if you add a rectangle around some object in order to visually group them together.
In such cases clicking and dragging always graps the rectangle (or whatever shape you used). There is no way to get the rectangle-selection it seems.

I tried shift-drag, ctrl-drag, alt-drag and many more, also searched for a selection tool in the toolbar, however couldn't find anything. [The only thing which works in such cases so far is to ctrl-click on the objects one after another, which brings them all to a single selection. But this is really not comparable to a rectanlge like selection tool.]

Suggestions:
1. make one of ``shift-drag``, or ``alt-drag``, or ``alt-shift-drag`` to always enable rectangle-like selection (independent of whether there is an object below or not). As ctrl-drag already has a selection related meaning in that it combines the single selections to one big selection (this already works with the rectangle selection and is a very great feature!) it would be great that if you at ``ctrl`` to the above modifier keys it also adds to the current selection.
1. add a set of selection tools to the toolbar

For the latter you might consider adding a free-hand selection tool, too, where you can freely draw the selection boundary.

Thanks for the possibility to suggest features!

* Operating system: Windows
* Pencil version: 3 RC1

title: Convert default connectors to separate connector objects immediately
body:
Dear Pencil Team,

a suggestion concerning the connectors which appear if you pull and drop a connector point from one object to a connector point of another object.
By default, this adds a curvy-like connector, however it is not an independent thing but belongs to the original object (rectangle or something) where the connector was pulled from.

This has several disadvantages:
- you cannot simply click on the connector for deletion in case it does not look like you want it (very common thing you may want to do) (the alternative is to pull from the target and drop the connector on an empty place, this deletes it apparently in my version, but I think this is not as intuitive as select and delete)
- you cannot simply change properties of the connector (like "slightly detached" or anything)
- you cannot add another connector to the connection point pulled from
Furthermore, I cannot see any advantages.

Directly inserting curvy connector object instead bypasses all the three mentioned disadvantages and hence I would suggest to do so.

title: Using controls without changing values affect the elements
body:
I have found multiple cases where using a control without actually changing any value or changing an irrelevant one can modify an element causing it to be "recalculated". This can cause problems such as issue #100.

What I mean by "calculation" includes the setting/changing of the sketchy line pattern and probably other values of the element.

To see it easily in action, use a sketchy Box since its borders' "recalculation" make it visually profound.
#### Toolbar Controls
1. Applying a shape format using the "Copy shape format" tool, even if nothing else changes.
2. Clicking on the "Background color" button, even without changing anything.
3. Clicking on the "Line color" button, even without changing anything.
4. Selecting a different "Line style", even when the line width is `0`
5. Changing the "Line width", even if you set it to the same width it was (ie not actually changing it). eg. start with width `0`, copy-paste the same width (still `0`) and the element gets recalculated.
6. Changing its location ("Left" or "Top") using any of the toolbar controls, even if set to the same value (like 5 above).
7. Changing its size ("Width" or "Height") using any of the toolbar controls, even if set to the same value (like 5 above).
8. Clicking inside the "Rotate" input, even if you don't change anything.
#### Properties Sidebar Controls

Exactly the same behavior as their toolbar counterparts.
1. Clicking on the "Background color" button.
2. Clicking on the "Line color" button.
3. Selecting a different "Line style".
4. Changing the "Line width".
#### Correct Behavior

None of the above should have the mentioned side effects.

Specifically, the sketchy line pattern should only change while effectively changing the size or on new/paste/clone of such elements so that the resulting drawing is more sketch-like instead of artificially looking.

title: Element bounding box should be consistent across shapes
body:
Currently there are multiple inconsistencies between the _real_ and _calculated_ bounding boxes (BB) of elements.
When I say _real_ I refer to the BB we get when the element is not part of a group. It is the BB that affects size and location.
On the other hand, when I say _calculated_ I am talking about the BB that affects the size and location when part of a group / multi-element selection.

This causes problems with resizing and moving grouped shapes, trying to match the size of different shapes etc. (see issue #100).
### Sketchy Shapes

As an example see the following screenshot of the really problematic case of sketchy shapes.

![bounding-box](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1144686/17737198/8fab6d76-6494-11e6-854b-35996bbe6dc7.PNG)

Their BB should always be the same; IMHO the _real_ one, to be consistent with non-sketchy elements (see below).

---
### Different Shapes - Different BBs

The following shapes have:
**size:** 80x80 px
**background color:** orange
**border color:** yellow semi-transparent
**border with:** 10px

I have overlayed both the _real_ (blue) and the _calculated_ (green) BBs.
The red dotted lines are guides for comparison.

_Open image in new window for full size._

![bb-comparison-multiselect](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1144686/17738786/73acec9c-649b-11e6-80ec-dd0cbe542298.PNG)

Assuming the CSS3 box-sizing property is used then we have different values for different shapes.
1. For example notice the smaller size of CS Rectangles which obviously account for the border while the rest of the shapes don't.
2. The BWE Pane has its border completely inside the shape while the rest of the shapes have it on top of their BB (half border in, half border out). Additionally notice the magical white space between the shape and its _calculated_ BB.
3. The _real_ vs _calculated_ BBs are all over the place. The prize in this category goes to CS Rectangle whose _calculated_ BB has different height and width.

---
### To Summarize

All shapes should have **consistent and predictable behavior**, preferably that of CS Oval. That is:
- The border should be around the shape's content (half in - half out).
- The border should not be included in the BBs.
- Both _real_ and _calculated_ BBs should match.

---
